assessment.nobel_worthiness: Melitz's heterogeneous-firm model changed how trade is studied. It moved the analysis from countries and industries to firms, with selection, reallocation and productivity gains from openness. It generated a large body of empirical work and a standard quantitative framework. This is a field-defining change in what we know and in how we measure it.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central contribution. Helpman's work on firm-level trade, including with Melitz and Yeaple on exports versus FDI, and on trade and inequality, is the natural co-recognition. Redding is important mainly for quantitative extensions and is left out to keep the prize focused. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum have strong claims and are outside this ballot entry's credited names, which complicates attribution.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of replication, microdata tests and policy use. The framework is established, so the timing is ripe.
uncertainties: Competing claims from Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum could make a narrower laureate set contested.
Whether the committee sees this as too close to the 2008 trade prize.
Some magnitudes of welfare gains are model-dependent.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kiyotaki and Moore show how collateral constraints amplify and propagate shocks into credit cycles. This is a foundational mechanism, and the 2008 crisis made it central to macroeconomics. It underlies much modern macro-finance and policy thinking on financial stability.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki-Moore (1997) is the core contribution. Gertler's work on the financial accelerator and on intermediary frictions is a closely related line. Bernanke, who shares the accelerator work with Gertler and Gilchrist, already received the 2022 prize for banks and financial crises, which weakens the accelerator side of the claim. Gilchrist is left out for that reason and because his role is more empirical.
assessment.maturity: Nearly thirty years of influence, a clear post-2008 vindication, and extensive empirical and quantitative follow-up. This is highly mature.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize and the Bernanke-Gertler-Gilchrist accelerator may split credit.
Direct empirical identification of the collateral channel is mixed.
A three-person limit forces a choice between the Gertler and Gilchrist lines.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic panel GMM estimators are among the most widely used empirical tools in economics, covering growth, firm and labour microdata. They make it possible to estimate dynamics with unobserved heterogeneity. This is a durable methodological contribution that changed practice across fields.
assessment.attribution: Arellano-Bond (1991), Arellano-Bover (1995) and Blundell-Bond (1998) form a clear triplet. Anderson-Hsiao and Holtz-Eakin, Newey and Rosen are important precursors. Hansen's GMM prize in 2013 provides the underlying framework, so the contribution is an applied extension of it.
assessment.maturity: More than thirty years of use and refinement. Known issues such as instrument proliferation and weak-instrument problems are well documented.
uncertainties: The contribution is a specialised extension of GMM, already recognised in 2013, which may weigh against it.
Blundell's wider labour and consumption work may blur attribution.
Known limits of the estimators, such as many instruments and weak identification.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantile regression extends analysis from conditional means to the full conditional distribution. It is essential for studying inequality, wage structure and heterogeneous effects. It is used widely in empirical work, including in economic history, where distributions matter. It is a clear and elegant methodological advance.
assessment.attribution: Koenker and Bassett (1978) introduced the estimator, and Koenker's later development of theory, computation and applications is substantial. Chernozhukov's contributions to inference and to causal and high-dimensional extensions are significant but belong to a different, later stage of the field.
assessment.maturity: Nearly fifty years of use, with standard software and textbook treatment. It is mature and uncontested as a tool.
uncertainties: The method is also developed and used in statistics, which may weigh on perceived economic-science relevance.
A two-laureate set excludes Chernozhukov, whose claim is arguably stronger in some areas.
Methods prizes are rarer than substantive ones.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework, with nominal rigidities, staggered pricing and rule-based monetary policy, underpins modern central banking and policy analysis. Its influence on real-world policy is large and direct.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is the main difficulty. Calvo (staggered pricing), Taylor (staggered contracts and the policy rule) and Woodford (the micro-founded synthesis) are the clearest individual contributions. Galí, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets and others made substantial and arguably co-equal contributions. Any three-name set is open to the objection that it leaves out others.
assessment.maturity: Decades of use in central banks, with strong empirical and policy testing. The framework was also stress-tested by the crisis and the post-2021 inflation, and this has led to refinements.
uncertainties: The diffuse credit among eight names makes a three-laureate selection contestable.
Debate over how well the framework performed in the 2008 crisis and the inflation of 2021-23.
Overlap with earlier macro prizes on expectations and monetary policy.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bayesian persuasion and information design give a general theory of how a designer's choice of information structure shapes behaviour. It extends mechanism design and information economics and applies to regulation, disclosure, platforms and policy.
assessment.attribution: Kamenica-Gentzkow (2011) is the core. Bergemann-Morris developed the general information-design and Bayes correlated equilibrium framework. Morris also has prior global-games work, which strengthens his case. Choosing three of four credited names is a judgement call, and Bergemann's claim is close to Morris's.
assessment.maturity: The theory is about fifteen years old. It is highly influential, but empirical validation and applied depth are still developing. The timing is somewhat early compared with the leading candidates.
uncertainties: The field may be seen as still maturing, with fewer decisive empirical applications.
Attribution among Bergemann, Morris, Kamenica and Gentzkow could divide the committee.
Gentzkow's separate empirical work on media may or may not strengthen the case.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The intertemporal approach to the current account and open-economy macroeconomics, in the Foundations of International Macroeconomics and the Obstfeld-Rogoff 1995 'redux' model, provided the micro-founded workhorse for international macro. Their exchange-rate disconnect puzzles also set a major research agenda.
assessment.attribution: A clear and compact pair with a long collaboration on the core texts and papers. Rogoff also appears on the financial-crisis history entry, which may split his case across ballots.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of influence, widely taught and used in policy institutions. The puzzles remain open, so empirical resolution is incomplete.
uncertainties: Overlap with other international macro and policy-oriented contributions.
Whether a micro-founded framework with unresolved puzzles is ranked above other candidates.
Rogoff's candidacy in multiple entries complicates how his credit is weighed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Misallocation across firms provides a measurable account of why total factor productivity and incomes differ across countries. It links micro-level distortions to aggregate income gaps and connects growth, development and industrial organisation. It also inspired a large measurement literature using new data.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh-Klenow (2009) and Restuccia-Rogerson (2008) are the two original papers. Rogerson is not credited on this ballot entry, which leaves the credit set incomplete. Selecting from Hsieh, Klenow and Restuccia is reasonable but imperfect.
assessment.maturity: About fifteen years of influence. Measurement debates about the size of the effect and about measurement error remain active, so the findings are still being refined.
uncertainties: Sensitivity of the estimated gains to measurement error and to the assumed model.
Omission of Rogerson from the credited names affects attribution.
A relatively recent contribution compared with the older candidates.
